entries.title: Library topics are a little less narrow
entries.body: The topics above your library take in an article that deals with a topic in substance, even when that is not its main subject, and a narrower topic can hold articles from outside the broader one. New articles are filed this way; existing topics change only when a library's topics are rebuilt, which is not every library at once.

entries.title: Glossary and Citations sit one place earlier
entries.body: In the bar at the bottom of an article, Glossary comes before FAQ and Citations before Referee. The Help icon is gone from that bar for the article's owner; Help is still reachable from the command bar and from the (i) beside a mode. A visitor, who has no command bar, keeps the Help link.

entries.title: A half-typed Chat question survives switching modes
entries.body: A question you had started typing in Chat was lost if you switched to another mode and came back. It is kept, and you return to the conversation you left, in Chat and in Remember's conversations. It is not kept if you reload the page.

entries.title: Citations reads raised reference numbers
entries.body: Citations lost the reference list in papers that cite with small raised numbers instead of numbers in square brackets. It can match them for articles added or re-processed after this change; existing results are not repaired. The matching is a rule of thumb, and can mistake a footnote or another numbered label for a citation.

entries.title: Endnote pages in PDFs are recognised as notes
entries.body: In some PDFs a page of endnotes came out as ordinary paragraphs, so the note numbers in the text did not link to their notes. A page like that can be recognised as notes when it follows a Notes or Endnotes heading. This applies to PDFs added or re-processed after this change; ones already in your library are not repaired.

entries.title: Unusual DOI links reach the right paper
entries.body: A DOI is the permanent identifier a publisher gives a paper. When one contained unusual characters, a link built from it could point to a different work. Links in Citations, in Debate's list of citing papers and in the card that appears when you point at a link are built correctly. This matters only for DOIs with unusual characters.
